applicable_when: The B matrix is stored as (40, 144) with stride_bk=1, stride_bn=144 (column-major in K). The load B[k + 144*n] with BLOCK_K=16 rows and BLOCK_N=64 columns accesses B with stride 144 elements (576 bytes) between consecutive N-elements. Since shared memory banks are 4 bytes wide with 32 banks (128-byte period), stride 144 = 576 bytes = 4.5x128 bytes creates a non-integer multiple of the bank period, causing systematic 11.9-way bank conflicts on every shared load. The fix is to load B as a transposed [BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K] tile (consecutive K-elements per N-row, stride=1, fully coalesced) then pass tl.trans(b_T) to tl.dot. All prior correctness failures came from incorrectly restructuring index arithmetic — this plan preserves ALL original A-load and output-store arithmetic, only changing the B load to use the transposed layout.

The fix is to pre-transpose B to [K=144, N=40] row-major layout (stride_bk=40, stride_bn=1) before launching, then update the kernel's B load pointer arithmetic to use contiguous strides. This eliminates the strided shared memory access entirely. Previous autotune attempts failed correctness because they changed tile sizes without preserving the exact index arithmetic — this plan does NOT change tile sizes, only the B matrix memory layout and corresponding load pointer.

strategy_title: Autotune num_stages/num_warps only regresses with bank conflicts
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune varying only num_stages (2, 3) and num_warps (4, 8) — with no change to tile sizes or memory access patterns — caused a 14.3% regression. Duration increased from 21.22 µs to 24.8 µs, Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction worsened from 4.44 to 5.37, IPC dropped from 0.88 to 0.75, and 'No Eligible' scheduler cycles increased from 77.53% to 81.29%. The shared memory bank conflict count remained essentially unchanged (11.9-way conflicts, ~77% conflict wavefronts), confirming that varying num_stages/num_warps alone cannot resolve bank conflicts caused by a fixed strided access pattern. This is a confirmed anti-pattern: when SharedMemoryConflicts dominates with >70% conflict wavefronts and MIO stalls account for >57% of warp stall cycles, the access stride pattern itself must be changed to reduce conflicts.
applicable_when: Never — this pattern (autotune num_stages/num_warps only, no tile or access pattern change) is a confirmed regression when shared memory bank conflicts are the dominant bottleneck.
do_not_apply_when: When SharedMemoryConflicts NCU rule fires with >70% conflict wavefronts and MIO stalls account for >57% of warp stall cycles, varying num_stages and num_warps alone cannot reduce bank conflicts. The access stride pattern must be changed (e.g., padding shared memory, transposing the tile layout, or rewriting the index arithmetic) to actually reduce conflicts. Do not apply when achieved occupancy is already at its ceiling due to grid size (123 blocks < 132 SMs) rather than warp/stage configuration.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune configs with empty dicts {} only vary num_stages and num_warps — they do NOT change tile sizes or memory access patterns. Bank conflicts are determined by the stride of shared memory accesses, which is fixed by the kernel's index arithmetic regardless of num_stages/num_warps. The autotuner overhead itself adds latency when no configuration can address the root bottleneck.
